items.title: UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada condemn Israel's West Bank settlement project
items.description: European countries and Canada pile on pressure over Israel's plans to expand settlements in a strategically vital part of the occupied West Bank.

items.title: How much could Trump's 'economic D-Day' hurt Iran?
items.description: Iran has so far proved adept at finding ways around years of already punishing sanctions on its economy.

items.title: El Niño set to be 'strongest in living memory', says Met Office
items.description: Scientists say the growing El Niño weather pattern is an "unprecedented event" and means 2027 is likely to be the world's hottest year on record.

items.title: Why the US economy is ringing alarm bells
items.description: The US hit a debt milestone this week, but just how worried should we be about the world's largest economy?

items.title: Hong Kong's Tiananmen activists guilty in national security trial
items.description: Three activists were accused of inciting others to subvert state power under the China-introduced law.

items.title: Bali jails Swiss tourist for insulting sacred Day of Silence
items.description: The 26-year-old sparked anger with an expletive-laden post about the sacred holiday.

items.title: Como mayor hit by electric bike and issues blanket ban in Italian city
items.description: Alessandro Rapinese said the prohibition was for public safety, adding "I know what it's like to be hit by one of these beasts".

items.title: Trump wants to be friends with Kim - but South Korea could pay the price
items.description: US military exercises with South Korea end early on Friday, at a time when the North is in a position of strength.

items.title: Russia 'purposefully' hit critical infrastructure in latest strikes, Kyiv mayor says
items.description: At least 17 people were killed in the "massive attack" overnight on Ukraine's capital, as mayor Vitali Klitschko warns hot water supply has been disrupted.

items.title: FBI arrests woman over alleged plot to bomb New York capitol building
items.description: Prosecutors say the Albany woman had pledged allegiance to the Islamic State group, and wanted to bomb the statehouse to kill lawmakers.

items.title: Jailed Pakistan ex-PM Imran Khan taken to hospital for treatment
items.description: Khan was taken from Adiala jail and sent to Shifa International Hospital under heavy security, according to his party.

items.title: US sanctions more Cuban companies and officials

items.title: Dozens dead after boat capsizes in north-western Nigeria
items.description: The incident took place in the country's northwest ​Sokoto state, with many of the victims feared to be children.

items.title: Belgian car salesman becomes prince after royal parentage confirmed
items.description: Clément Vandenkerckhove was quietly brought into Prince Laurent's family at a town hall ceremony.

items.title: Giant whales move into Greenland waters as ice disappears

items.title: Assad officer extradited to Syria on war crimes charges for first time
items.description: Lebanon handed over former General Adel Issa, as Syria steps up its pursuit of wanted members of the former regime.

items.title: Founder of collapsed Chinese property giant Evergrande sentenced to life in prison
items.description: Hui's sentencing marks a key moment in the fallout from Evergrande's collapse, which shook China's property sector.

items.title: German neo-Nazi suspected of deadly 1970 fire at Jewish retirement home
items.description: Investigators believe they have identified an arsonist who attacked a Jewish community centre in Munich in 1970, killing seven people.

items.title: Togo charges two French journalists over incorrect documents, rights group says
items.description: Gaël Mocaër and Sebastian Perez Pezzani's detention is "unjustified and disproportionate", Reporters Without Borders says.

items.title: Mushroom killer must stay in jail forever for 'truly dreadful' crime, appeal court told
items.description: Prosecutors say Erin Patterson's sentence was "manifestly inadequate" as it allows for the possibility of parole.
